text: Today, we celebrated a major milestone for the U.S. defense industrial base: the groundbreaking of AVIO USA's first solid rocket motor manufacturing facility. title: Vassilis Diakoloukas • 3-й+
text: 𝗪𝗲 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝘂𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗻 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗱𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀!! I'm incredibly proud to share that our team won the MathWorks Minidrone Competition Europe! Out of around 70 teams from leading universities across Europe, we made it to the top 5 finalists and earned our place in the grand final at the MathWorks offices in Cambridge, UK. After two days of intense competition, technical challenges, and real-world drone testing, we came home with 1st place! The challenge was to develop a fully autonomous drone capable of navigating an unknown track, making real-time decisions, and landing smoothly and accurately at its destination without relying on a predefined map. Our solution combined computer vision, path planning, and autonomous control. We developed a multi-ring search algorithm to identify the path ahead and determine the drone's direction and speed, along with a trajectory memory mechanism to prevent it from revisiting sections of the track it had already completed. Landing was a challenge of its own. We developed a vision-based algorithm to recognize the landing target, distinguish it from the track, and position the drone accurately above it. But getting everything to work in simulation was only half the job! For the final, we had to adapt our algorithms to run on a real drone with limited onboard processing power, memory, and strict real-time requirements. We redesigned our navigation system around a much lighter single-ring search, reduced the trajectory memory, and simplified the landing approach. The drone could identify the landing target, align itself with its center, lock its horizontal position, and perform a smooth, controlled descent. I've attached a video showing our work in action, from the initial simulation and our multi-ring path planning and trajectory memory algorithms to the final real-world flight. I would like to thank my teammates Athanasios Digkas , Dimitrios Ioannidis , and Marios Antakis for all the hard work and dedication in this incredible experience. I would also like to thank MathWorks and especially Krishna Keerthana Chiruvolu and Manjunath R for organizing the competition and hosting us in Cambridge. It was a fantastic experience and a great opportunity to meet talented students from across Europe! #MathWorks #MinidroneCompetition #Robotics #AutonomousSystems #ComputerVision #AI #Engineering
author: Vassilis Diakoloukas • 3-й+
